speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination. To begin my assessment, have you noticed any pain or burning during urination, or is the frequency the only symptom?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; the relief of discomfort with voiding and the recent onset of dyspareunia are significant clues. Have you noticed any visible blood in your urine, or have you experienced any pelvic pain unrelated to urination?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome.
